status: In text.json as Fable's hand edits: the row carries `hand`, its mark naming both rounds, so no run of the style loop replaces it (guide /17). Not scored: a judge run needs Sky's approval. The /18 busy tell (short-hand18.ts SUMMON_18) already lists every case, "with her" among them, so a later judge run could check this round; this round read each line in every case below, before each of the guard's two replies and alone. Three more changes in the same round sit outside the loop's families, so they have no entry in `edits`. Aster took Keel's option (b) (briefs/102/keel/call-offer.md): a Call is offered only where it has a use under the rules, so in the Handover neither the turned guard nor the turned driver will be offered one (Keel and Latch build it later). Scripted orders and other missions can still reach the no-visit refusal, so its words must hold for whoever is called. (1) locks.summon-no-visit, the refusal of a call on a contact whose tie can't come (in the Handover, the Fixer's Call on the turned guard): line "Their lover has no post to leave, so this call moves no one." -> "Calling {who} brings nobody.", short "No post to leave" -> "Nobody comes". "Lover" named what only a Listen teaches (people.rules secrets.list.affair: the tie is the secret, and Listen alone teaches it), and "no post to leave" was false: Inez has her place at the café. Today the words show on the Call card's lock before the click (HandoverHost.cs CallLock, from Game.CallQuery), on the pop at the click, and as the footer of the refused card, under the guard's line and Inez's reply when she hears it (HostFeed.cs FeedSummonRefused). They name whoever was called, never the one they'd send for, and say only what the call does: nobody comes and nobody goes, wherever either of them stands and whatever state the tie is in. That reads like any call that does nothing, so a cell that turned the contact without a Listen learns nothing of the two of them (the Handover's briefing already says the Fixer calls Inez to draw the guard off the door). No fix in it: "Call Inez" would be false or no use when the guard is already off the door, when she has called him once, when she can't be called, or in another mission. (2) locks.already-turned (Keel's finding; Ask, Pay or Pressure on a contact already turned, GameOrders.cs NeedsNo): line "{who} is already turned. Call them, or Help to keep them on side." -> "{who} is already turned. No need to turn them again.", short "Already turned" kept. "Call them" was false for the guard and the driver, whose calls do nothing and who will be offered none, and Help is shut for anyone whose need is met, untold, or not one Help meets (rulebook turn.help needs; on a turned contact it plays its `kept` outcome only when it is open). The new line holds for any turned contact, whether or not a Call is offered, and the card shows what is still open. (3) Cut from less.pop, which no code reads (Aster checked Runtime/ for literal and computed lookups: PopKey, Pops.TryGetValue, HostFight's P; Fable checked Runtime, sim and tools again): camera-hit ("Camera hit": a hit that doesn't put a camera out stays silent, a pulse on it, HandoverHost.cs CameraShot), camera-looped ("Camera looped": the Loop's chip reads less.done.gain.camera-looped, which stays), select-agent ("Select an agent": the panel writes its own note, HandoverHost.cs) and stand-after-vale ("After Popovic's car": the host writes the yard's words itself, HostDriveCar.cs). Their pins in text.test.ts (select-agent, camera-looped) went with them.
why: Aster, 2026-11-09 (to brief 102's bar), yes to the three things Fable raised: the guard's no-visit refusal gave away the secret, Inez's busy lines play while the guard is already beside her, and four pop words had no caller. Then, on Keel's proposal: the no-visit words for whoever a script or another mission calls, and Keel's finding that `already-turned` promised a Call. When Inez's busy lines play: the Fixer's Call on her is refused summon-busy (sim GameOrders.cs SummonRefusal) when the guard is down (knocked out, tied or dead), held (just come round and walking back, fighting the rivals, drawing on the cell, searching for the shooter, wounded), engaged in a fight (at his door too), or away on her last call (walking over, standing with her at the café, walking or running back). She answers the Fixer on the telephone in every one, and the guard answers her after it, "Can't oblige, I'm afraid." or "Not now, Inez. I'm on duty.", unless he is down (HostFeed.cs FeedSummonRefused, TieHears). The host picks her line and his apart (PlayText.Pick), so each of hers must hold in every case: before either of his, and alone. Neither may say where he is, or what she knows.

edits.before: You've picked your moment, dear. He can't.
edits.why: "He can't" is false when he can and does: walking over to her, or beside her at the café on her last call. Her wry first sentence is true in every case: the moment is wrong whether he is down, coming round, in a fight or with her, and it says nothing of where he is or what she knows. Before his "Can't oblige, I'm afraid." or "Not now, Inez. I'm on duty." it is her aside and then his answer; alone, when he is down, it stands.

edits.before: You'll not get him now for love nor money.
edits.why: "You'll not get him now" is false when he is on his way to her or already beside her. The idiom alone keeps her café patter, money in it, and is true in every case: no call brings him now. No "dear", so the two lines don't end alike. It leads into either of his lines, and stands alone.
